name: Livadeia
locality: Livadia Municipality; Commune of Levadia, Viotia
text: Livadeia (Greek: Λιβαδειά [livaˈðja]; Ancient Greek: Λεβάδεια [lebádeːa]) is a town in central Greece. It is the capital of the Boeotia regional unit. Livadeia lies 90 km (56 mi) north-west of Athens, 64 km (40 mi) west of Chalkida, 63 km (39 mi) south-east of Lamia, 44 km (27 mi) east-south-east of Amfissa, and 91 km (57 mi) east-north-east of Nafpaktos.

depictions.name: Lebadeia
depictions.text: Livadeia Lebadeia (Ancient Greek: Λεβάδεια) is a town in Greece. In classical antiquity, it was a polis located in the Reborn Hills region of Boeotia. In antiquity, Lebadeia was famous for its oracle of the mythical hero Trophonios.
